newsitem.title: UK: Highland disturbed by French duty rise.
newsitem.headline: Highland disturbed by French duty rise.

text.p: Scotch Whisky distiller Highland Distilleries chief executive Brian Ivory said a 17 percent duty rise on spirits sold in France signals a disturbing Euro-trend.
"There are disturbing trends in European duty rates, namely in France," Ivory told reporters. France is Highland's largest export market, with around 10 percent of its export sales.

France will raise duty paid on spirits by 17 percent from January, while leaving duty on beer unchanged. No duty is paid on wine. The change will put five or six francs on a bottle of Famous Grouse, Highland's leading blended whisky, making it about 85 or 87 francs a bottle, said Ivory.

Although the duty increase also applies to Cognac, Whisky outsells Cognac by about six or seven bottles to one in France, said Ivory. However, Ivory could not say what the impact was likely to be on Famous Grouse sales.
"The French are doing the job of harmonisation for us. Our duty rate should be coming down but in fact the French are raising theirs," said Ivory.

The Scotch Whisky Association estimates that in the UK, a standard blended bottle of whisky costs 10.70 stg. Excise duty strips out 5.54 stg, value-added tax 1.59 stg, making the total tax take 67 percent or 7.13 stg.

In France, where the same bottle costs about 8.65 stg, the current tax take is 56 percent and in Greece, where duties were raised recently, a bottle costs 7.0 stg with 42 percent going in tax. In Spain, a bottle costs 6.30 stg and just 39 percent goes in tax.
